t: You're standing where Prince's Cricket Ground once stood in Chelsea. It was laid out by the brothers George and James Prince as part of the Prince's Club, on the former Cattleugh's nursery gardens. Thirty-seven matches were played here between 1872 and 1878, and the site was built on in 1883. Its edges are still traced by Cadogan Square West, Milner Street, Lennox Gardens Mews, Walton Street and Pont Street. Thomas Box died here in 1876. He is remembered as one of the most outstanding wicketkeepers of the nineteenth century.
